outcomes: A workload that owns several schemas of one physical database holds one connection pool for that database, so its idle backends and connection ceiling scale with databases, not with datasources
Every unqualified query a datasource issues resolves in that datasource's schema, whichever datasource last used the pooled connection
Reserved connections and driver transactions stay bound to their datasource, so the transaction machinery and the migrator keep their search_path on the shared pool
Closing one datasource never interrupts another datasource of the same database
nonGoals: Sharing a pool across different connection identities (different host, database, user, or password source)
Reconciling different pool tunings declared for one database by taking the largest
Guarding user code that issues a session-level SET search_path, RESET, or DISCARD ALL on a framework connection
Changing how transactions are keyed: useTxConnection and UnitOfWork stay keyed by datasource

text: The pool carries no search_path startup parameter and records the search_path each connection's session holds, forgetting it on a close, a reserve() or a transaction;
an operation sends its statement alone when its connection holds the datasource's path, else first awaits set_config('search_path', $1, false), or RESET search_path for the server default;
a failed set rejects the operation before its statement is sent.
database(name) returns a datasource-bound client, never the shared driver pool: tagged-template queries, unsafe, file and notify set the path when their connection does not hold it;
reserve() and begin() set it on the pinned connection they hand out;
a query used as a fragment of another runs on that other query's connection;
cancel and query modes reach the inner driver query;
identifier and row builders are made by the physical pool and touch no connection.

requirements.text: Physical pools are keyed by the effective connection identity of each datasource — host, port, database, resolved username, password source, ssl and the remaining startup parameters — never by datasource name: byte-identical identities share one physical pool, distinct identities open distinct pools, and concurrent first opens of one identity connect once.

Datasource-bound clients hold references on their physical pool: closing one datasource leaves the shared pool open for the others, closing the last handle ends it, a closed client rejects its operations with an error, closeAllDatabases ends every pool, and a later database(name) re-opens.

text: Datasources that resolve to one physical pool must declare the same poolSize, connectTimeout, idleTimeout, maxLifetime, statementTimeoutMs, idleInTransactionTimeoutMs and debug;
a difference rejects database(name) with an error naming both datasources and each differing field, never a larger ceiling or a second pool.
A physical pool opens a connection only when every connection it holds is leased and it holds fewer than poolSize;
an operation that finds poolSize connections leased waits for one to be released, and the most recently released connection is reused first.

requirements.text: Each connection of a physical pool closes after maxLifetime seconds; when maxLifetime is 0, each connection draws a lifetime between 45 and 90 minutes, so a long-running workload recycles its connections and the prepared statements they hold.
